overview: The Kushan Empire was a syncretic Central Asian power that facilitated Silk Road trade between Rome, China and India. It patronized Buddhism, created the unique Greco-Buddhist Gandhara art style and issued widely circulated gold coinage.

items.text: Gandharan art blends Greek, Roman and Indian styles to create the first anthropomorphic representations of the Buddha.
Monumental Buddhist monasteries and stupas constructed across modern Pakistan and Afghanistan.
Controlled major Silk Road routes connecting the Mediterranean, Central Asia, India and China.
Gold coinage facilitated international commerce and advertised the king's divine status.
Kanishka convenes the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir, promoting Mahayana Buddhism.
Zoroastrianism, Greek religion, Hinduism and Buddhism all practiced within the empire.
Gandharan Buddhist art influenced Central Asian and East Asian religious art for centuries.
The empire's multicultural character exemplified Silk Road civilization at its peak.

fall.text: The Kushan Empire fragmented under pressure from the Gupta Empire and Sasanian Persia.
